description: The bar chart illustrates five distinct layer grouping patterns—labeled Increasing, Uniform, Decreasing, Spindle, and Bottleneck—used in parameter-efficient fine-tuning design spaces, where the horizontal axis represents four sequential groups (G₁ to G₄) and the vertical axis indicates the number of layers assigned to each group. In the “Increasing” pattern, the bar heights rise progressively from left to right: G₁ has the fewest layers (~1 unit), G₂ slightly more (~2 units), G₃ even more (~3 units), and G₄ the most (~4 units). The “Uniform” pattern shows four bars of equal height (~3 units each), indicating an even distribution of layers across all groups. The “Decreasing” pattern mirrors the “Increasing” one in reverse: G₁ has the most layers (~4 units), followed by G₂ (~3 units), G₃ (~2 units), and G₄ the fewest (~1 unit). The “Spindle” pattern features a central peak: G₁ and G₄ have the fewest layers (~1 unit), while G₂ and G₃ are taller and equal (~3 units each), forming a symmetrical bulge. The “Bottleneck” pattern shows G₁ and G₄ with moderate height (~3 units), while G₂ and G₃ are shorter and equal (~2 units), creating a narrow middle section. All bars are rendered in light green with black outlines, and the chart uses no numerical scale on the vertical axis, relying instead on relative bar heights to convey the number of layers per group.
